name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
licenseNote: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 is a United States government publication in the public domain. AEGIS references function and category identifiers only; every title and summary is original AEGIS wording describing the outcome and is not the text of the framework. Mapping an AEGIS record to a category here is not a conformance statement.
description: The six functions of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) at category level, with the AEGIS records that evidence each for AI agents.

controls.title: Organizational context
controls.summary: The organization's mission, stakeholders, legal obligations and dependencies that shape cybersecurity risk decisions are understood and recorded.

controls.title: Risk management strategy
controls.summary: Priorities, risk appetite and assumptions are set and communicated so operational risk decisions, including those about AI systems, are consistent.

controls.title: Roles, responsibilities and authorities
controls.summary: Leadership is accountable for cybersecurity risk and roles are assigned, resourced and understood.

controls.title: Policy
controls.summary: Cybersecurity policy is established, communicated, enforced and reviewed as risks and requirements change.

controls.title: Oversight
controls.summary: Results of risk management activities are reviewed to adjust strategy and improve performance.

controls.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management
controls.summary: Suppliers and third-party services, including AI models and connectors, are identified, assessed, contracted and monitored for cybersecurity risk.

controls.title: Asset management
controls.summary: Hardware, software, services, data and the people and systems that act on them, including AI agents, are inventoried and prioritised.

controls.title: Risk assessment
controls.summary: Vulnerabilities, threats and the likelihood and impact of events are assessed to inform priorities and responses.

controls.title: Improvement
controls.summary: Lessons from assessments, tests, exercises and incidents feed improvements to processes and controls.

controls.title: Identity management, authentication and access control
controls.summary: Identities and credentials for people, services and agents are managed, authenticated strongly and granted access on need, with reviews and prompt removal.

controls.title: Awareness and training
controls.summary: People are trained to recognise and fulfil their cybersecurity responsibilities, including those who operate or approve for AI agents.

controls.title: Data security
controls.summary: Data at rest, in transit and in use is protected in line with its classification, including what agents send to external systems.

controls.title: Platform security
controls.summary: Hardware, software and services are configured, maintained, logged and changed under control.

controls.title: Technology infrastructure resilience
controls.summary: Networks and environments are segmented and protected, and capacity and continuity are maintained.

controls.title: Continuous monitoring
controls.summary: Assets, networks, services and activity, including what agents do, are monitored to find anomalies and potentially adverse events.

controls.title: Adverse event analysis
controls.summary: Anomalies and indicators are analysed and correlated to decide whether an incident has occurred and how severe it is.

controls.title: Incident management
controls.summary: Responses to declared incidents are managed under a plan with clear ownership, triage and escalation.

controls.title: Incident analysis
controls.summary: Incidents are investigated to establish what happened, its scope and its root cause, with records kept.

controls.title: Incident response reporting and communication
controls.summary: Internal and external stakeholders, including regulators where required, are informed of incidents as planned.

controls.title: Incident mitigation
controls.summary: Incidents are contained and eradicated, for example by suspending an agent, revoking a credential or pausing a gateway.

controls.title: Incident recovery plan execution
controls.summary: Operations are restored under a plan, with integrity of restored assets verified before use.

controls.title: Incident recovery communication
controls.summary: Recovery progress and completion are communicated to the people and parties who depend on the affected systems.
